title: NFSMW Setup JSON-line event
description: One object per stdout line with --events. Child output goes only to the run log. --check ends after preflight, pc, x360 with exit 0 and no done event; --build emits done only after verified transactional install. Stages in order: preflight, pc, x360, recompile, tables, audio, shaders, ffmpeg, runtime, assets, bundle, install. Audio builds its FFmpeg prerequisite before compiling media.cpp. Cancellation exits 130; every other failed stage exits nonzero. work/run-log.txt contains the current log path. Environment overrides: NFSMW_SETUP_HOME (state/logs/cache/data beneath it), NFSMW_SETUP_STATE, NFSMW_SETUP_LOGS, NFSMW_SETUP_CACHE, NFSMW_SETUP_DATA, NFSMW_SETUP_LEGACY (the 3.x profile whose career saves install copies into a 4.0 profile without saves; warn event on copy or refusal). --check logs only in work/logs. setup.sh uses TOOLS_PY, else deps/python/bin/python3, python/bin/python3 or .venv/bin/python3 in the payload. Public bundle: NFS Most Wanted Native.app (executable NFSMostWanted; an existing 3.x app there is renamed NFS Most Wanted Native 3.x.app and kept); io.github.nfsmw-native-mac; version 4.0.0. --stage-only --dest <installed .app path> --stage <new directory> [--work <build directory>] --events builds and verifies the full app/data without installation, recovery, profile locks or save migration. --pc may name a PC disc image (an .iso, or a mounted disc; the set's other discs are found beside it), installed into work/pc_src, with --pc-update (the official 1.3 update, applied without running it), --pc-exe (a speed.exe with the 1.3 code) and --pc-disc (repeatable: a disc of the set from any folder; discs are identified by content); these are refused with anything else. Omitted --pc/--x360/--dest reuse state/source-choices.json (with a remembered --pc, its remembered --pc-update, --pc-exe and --pc-disc too), saved atomically after successful normal Setup; a remembered Xbox source is never implicitly dropped. Missing choices/source errors name SOURCE_CHOICES_MISSING, SOURCE_CHOICES_INVALID, X360_SOURCE_MISSING or X360_PREPARATION_MISSING in msg. Staging replaces the install stage with stage and ends with ready (never done). The descriptor path is absolute. ready.json format_version=1 contains version, app/data paths and roots relative to its directory, hashes.app/data (install.digest_tree), hashes.roots (SHA256 of relative roots.txt), destination (path, filesystem identity and content hash), profile and provenance (original source paths, input hashes, executable fingerprint, source inventory identity, dependencies and toolchain). All staged files/directories are fsynced before the atomic descriptor publication. A stage directory must be new, distinct from all protected paths; retry in a fresh directory. Consumers must revalidate hashes and destination identity before application. Staging never rewrites remembered choices. --work defaults to a sibling .<stage-name>-work directory. A successful stage retains its build work for retry; only ready.json signals readiness. --export-all-in-one --app <installed .app> --dest <new .app> [--work <directory>] exports the current asset roots without changing profile preferences or remembered source choices. It emits bundle, warn (elapsed time and measured disk use), then done after final signing and verification. Existing destinations are refused. APFS clonefile is attempted per file; unsupported or cross-volume copies are SHA-256 verified. Contents/Resources/AllInOne/roots.txt contains bundle-relative pc_root, x360_root, assets_root and movies when installed. Export updates are refused: Re-export from Setup to update; retain the previous export for rollback. Standalone extras: --cars-check --carbon <folder|exe|ISO> recognizes Carbon without a compiler or MW build arguments. --cars-spec <JSON array> optionally plans permanent-slot metadata via F-T; --cars-measure measures conversion without activation. --cars-import requires --carbon and --cars-spec, using the installed roots.txt/app.txt MW donor root; --cars-mw-pc may explicitly supply donors before installation. --cars-list, --cars-remove <slot...>, and --cars-restore <g-SHA256> manage <installed-data>/car-catalog. --cars-repair retries rejected preparations from original inputs. Retained preparations live in <cache>/cars. Extras never read or write career saves or alter later-game settings (default Off). No build/preflight or PC rebuild flags are required or accepted. cars-recognition distinguishes verified source pairs from packaged output approval; cars-plan uses F-T per-volume bytes, retaining null for unknown output sizes. cars-progress extraction counters are bytes; converted/prepared/verification counters are completed boundaries. A cars-result terminates a successful operation and is never installation done. Recognition alone never verifies output. Failure exits nonzero, cancellation exits 130, with an error event and no cars-result/done. Retried imports reuse verified cache; remove retains generations for restore. Optional sources never replace the required MW PC/X360 inputs or remembered stage choices. cars-plan.cars lists each selected permanent slot, local display name, source hash, cache reuse, output approval and refusal reason. An unverified retained generation may have an invalid directory name; only verified g-SHA256 generations can be restored. A cancellation observed before publication retains the last-good pointer; a mutating cars-result with exit 0 reports an already committed change even if Cancel was clicked during completion. This never signals installation success.
